subject.title: [Bug]: replay_invalid thinking-signature crashes on process restart: 3 findings from 2026-07-03

question: Should OpenClaw solve this as a broad Anthropic replay-policy change, a narrow replay_invalid retry repair, or a split fix with config-write/session-lock handled separately?
rationale: Current source confirms the reported gap, but the best durable behavior depends on Anthropic replay policy and whether direct config-file writes during active sessions should be blocked, warned, or debounced.

options.title: Coordinate replay policy first
options.body: Adopt a cluster-level fix that strips or prunes stale completed-turn thinking while preserving current tool-turn signatures, then handle the config-write/session-lock behavior as a separate decision.

options.title: Narrow retry repair
options.body: Add a one-shot replay_invalid strip-and-retry path for this symptom, accepting that broader thinking replay policy may still need follow-up.

options.title: Split config-lock handling
options.body: Treat the replay bug and exec-path config-write/session-lock cascade as separate issues so the replay fix can land without deciding config hot-reload semantics in the same change.

recommendation.title: Coordinate replay policy first
recommendation.body: Adopt a cluster-level fix that strips or prunes stale completed-turn thinking while preserving current tool-turn signatures, then handle the config-write/session-lock behavior as a separate decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The replay-preservation policy for Claude Sonnet/Opus 4.x models is central to the product choice here.
